issues: Base image includes full Python distribution with unnecessary build tools and packages
No .dockerignore exclusion for docs/, tests/, ai_tools/, and other non-runtime directories
Single-stage build includes development dependencies and source files not needed at runtime
No multi-stage build to separate build and runtime environments
Unnecessary copying of entire repository due to incomplete .dockerignore
No use of slim or distroless base image for reduced attack surface
No cache optimization for dependency installation
recommended_changes: Use python:3.11-slim as base image to reduce size
Add docs/, tests/, ai_tools/, .github/, README.md, and similar to .dockerignore
Implement multi-stage build: first stage for dependencies, second for runtime
Create and use a non-root user (e.g., appuser) in the final image
Copy only requirements.txt and install dependencies in first stage
Copy only the app/ directory in final stage
Use slim or distroless image in final stage
Optimize layer caching by separating dependency install from code copy
Add user and group creation with proper permissions
expected_effect: Significant reduction in image size (expected 70-90% decrease)
Reduced number of layers and improved build cache efficiency
Faster cold and warm builds due to better layer caching
Decreased attack surface with fewer vulnerabilities
Elimination of critical and high severity Trivy findings in base image
Improved startup time due to smaller image
Better security posture from non-root execution
No negative impact on runtime functionality
More reliable builds due to explicit dependency isolation
Compliance with container security best practices
security_considerations: Running as root increases privilege escalation risk if container is compromised
Large base image includes unnecessary packages that may contain vulnerabilities
Exposure of build tools and development files in runtime image
Potential information leakage through included source and test files
Lack of healthcheck prevents orchestration systems from detecting unhealthy containers
No user namespace remapping in current configuration
Incomplete .dockerignore may lead to accidental inclusion of sensitive files
Use of latest tag equivalent (implicit) in base image reduces reproducibility
No vulnerability scanning in build pipeline indicated
No read-only root filesystem or dropped capabilities
verification_commands: docker run --rm -d -p 8000:8000 --name test-container rewriter-optimized && sleep 2 && docker ps && docker stop test-container
docker run --rm -p 8000:8000 rewriter-optimized & sleep 3 && curl -s http://localhost:8000/health || echo 'Health check failed' && kill $!
